findings.title: No double-check after acquiring write lock leads to redundant work and thundering herd on cache miss
findings.body: After acquiring entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() (line 48), the code does not re-check whether entryPointAssetsCache was already populated by another goroutine that got the lock first. Every goroutine that passed the initial RLock-based nil check will proceed to recompute the result (reading the manifest file or hitting the CDN) even though another goroutine may have just finished populating the cache. Under concurrent initial access (e.g. many simultaneous requests hitting GetWebAssets before the cache is warm), this causes redundant file reads and, worse, redundant outbound HTTP requests to the CDN in readWebAssetsFromCDN, which is both wasteful and could amplify load on an external CDN endpoint.

findings.title: Write lock held across blocking I/O (file read / HTTP call) serializes all callers
findings.body: The entryPointAssetsCacheMu write lock (acquired at line 48 and released via defer at line 49) is held for the entire duration of readWebAssetsFromFile/readWebAssetsFromCDN, including a network round-trip when a CDN URL is configured. While this does fix the data race, it means every concurrent call to GetWebAssets that misses the cache (or is in Dev mode, which always recomputes) will serialize behind a potentially slow network call, which can increase request latency under load compared to a design that only locks around the shared variable assignment.

findings.title: No regression test added for the data race fix
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race on the global entryPointAssetsCache variable but does not add any test (e.g. a test exercising GetWebAssets concurrently, ideally run with -race) to verify the fix or guard against future regressions. Without such a test, a future refactor could easily reintroduce the race undetected.
